subject: Clearwave: retention exception & cross-border proof request
messages:
From: Emily Wong <emily.wong@clearwave.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Cc: legal@clearwave.com
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Request: retention exception + subprocessors evidence for DPA addendum

Hi Tessa,

We're reviewing the DPA addendum draft and have a couple of asks before we can sign:

1) Retention exception: our clinical ingestion team needs confirmation that telemetry and debug traces can be excluded from customer PII retention exhibit. Can you confirm whether Redwood can apply an "escape-hatch" retention policy for non-PII telemetry (timestamps, request IDs, latency metrics) and supply an annotated field-level mapping?

2) Subprocessor proof: we need a current subprocessor roster with locations and explicit cross-border transfer justifications for any non-US subprocessors (or confirmation there are none).

3) Data flow diagram: for the production inference path (model proxy -> GPU pool -> logs/telemetry), can you provide an updated diagram that shows where PII is tokenized/redacted and where ephemeral caches exist? A simple PDF is fine.

Our legal/privacy review would like those artifacts by EOB Thursday (9/23) if possible. Happy to schedule a 30 min call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Wong
Head of Privacy Operations
Clearwave Health
[Attachment: cw_dpa_addendum_v1.docx (docx)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Wong <emily.wong@clearwave.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com, paul@privacyconsult.com
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Clearwave evidence package + proposed DPA addendum language

Emily — attaching the artifacts you requested. Summary below, and included attachments/links:

Summary (high level)
- Retention escape-hatch: We can implement a retention profile scoped to non-PII telemetry (request IDs, latency metrics, debug traces) that will be excluded from customer PII exhibits. The profile is implemented as a processing rule (retention_profile: "telemetry-ephemeral") and we will add the proposed language in the addendum.

- Field-level mapping: attached retention_mapping.csv (column: field_name | classification | retention_tier | notes). Fields marked as "telemetry" are candidate for the escape-hatch; fields marked "PII" are subject to the standard DPA retention schedule.

- Subprocessor roster: included in the roster tab of retention_mapping.csv and summarized below. No production inference subprocessors are located in jurisdictions requiring additional transfer mechanisms other than SCCs; where applicable we reference SCCs or equivalent transfer legal bases.

- Annotated dataflow: attached redwood_dataflow_v2.pdf — callouts show tokenization and redaction points, where KV caches live (ephemeral TTLs by shard), and where logs/telemetry are emitted to our telemetry sink.

Attachments included:
- redwood_dataflow_v2.pdf (annotated PDF)
- dpa_addendum.docx (proposed wording for retention escape-hatch)
- retention_mapping.csv (field-level mapping + subprocessor roster tab)

Related links:
- Evidence bundle (internal redwood drive): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/clearwave/retention-evidence
- Addendum signing (DocuSign): https://app.docusign.com/CLR-4532/addendum

Next steps / asks from you:
- Let us know if the proposed addendum wording covers the operational scope you need. If you want the telemetry profile enabled for a short pilot window we can toggle it in a dedicated tenant and provide screenshots of configuration.
- If legal needs SCC text inserted inline, share the target jurisdiction and we will add references.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20 min call Friday if that helps finalize.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
